parsed.explanation: The national regime creates direct visitor-facing risks: officers may refuse entry over sex-related discrepancies and may consider a permanent fraud finding, while trans and nonbinary travellers have reportedly been stranded after passport problems. The national restriction on gender-congruent facilities also applies, and this jurisdiction has an additional facilities ban with a documented arrest and 24-hour placement of a transgender woman in a men’s ward. The local ban’s scope and visitor enforcement are not established, so I do not assume every facility encounter leads to arrest. Nor does the record establish routine detention or that hostile counterterrorism language targets trans identity alone. Still, border exposure, an operative facilities restriction, and documented hostile enforcement place this materially below a jurisdiction with only social friction or latent rules; litigation and uncertainty do not remove those exposures.
